title: Investigate and fix duplicated token counts after quota-retry backfills in per-customer model charts
creator: Morgan Chen
description:
Summary:
Several customers reported that their per-model token usage in the Console shows inflated counts after a recent backfill of delayed usage events. The spike correlates with quota-retry and ingest-replay windows when rate-limited requests were re-enqueued.

Observed behavior:
- Console charts show day-level and model-level token counts 1.6x-2x higher than expected for affected accounts during the backfill window.
- The issue appears only when backfilled events are processed after rate-limit retries; real-time traffic without retries is unaffected.
- Downstream billing pipelines currently trust the merged timeseries produced by the Usage Ingest service; duplicates there propagate to per-route breakdowns and to the billing ledger.

Hypothesis and root cause (investigation so far):
- Rate limiter retries create new request records with a new internal request_id but preserve the same customer idempotency token in some paths; the backfill worker that replays delayed events originally did not populate the ingestion dedupe key consistently.
- The ingestion pipeline's de-duplication was keyed by (external_request_id, model_name, timestamp_bucket) for live traffic, but the backfill path used (event_id) which allowed duplicate external_request_id records to be stored when the retry created a distinct event_id.
- Console aggregation queries aggregate by model_name + day_bucket and sum token_count; duplicated rows lead to double-counting at both model and account scopes.

Work to do:
1) Add strict dedupe key alignment across live ingest and backfill paths: enforce canonical idempotency_id evaluated as (customer_id + external_request_id) and persisted on event write.
2) Update backfill worker to populate idempotency_id when replaying events and to use upsert semantics rather than blind insert.
3) Add a short-circuit in the Usage Ingest service to ignore events older than 72 hours unless they include a backfill flag and dedupe id.
4) Patch Console aggregation SQL to dedupe on idempotency_id at the materialized view level to prevent immediate double-counting until one full re-ingest completes.
5) Run a safe reingest of the backfilled window with dedupe enabled and validate counts against raw request logs and billing ledger.
6) Add regression test that simulates rate-limited retry + backfill to prevent recurrence.

Acceptance criteria (what "Done" looks like):
- Ingest pipeline dedupe key is consistent across regular and backfill paths and deployed to staging and prod feature-flagged.
- Backfill worker updated to upsert and/or dedupe on idempotency_id.
- Console per-model and account-level charts remove the duplication for the affected window (close to parity with raw request logs within 0.5%).
- Regression test included in the CI pipeline that simulates a retry+backfill and asserts no double-counts.
- Postmortem and runbook note added to the incident docs explaining how to scope and re-run safe backfills.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Reingest will re-run a potentially large volume of events; we'll throttle to avoid surcharge and coordinate with billing to mark the reingest as non-billable until validated.
- Materialized view dedupe may add cost/latency for Console queries; we will use a short-lived feature flag and monitor query latency.
- Tight dedupe rules could hide legitimate duplicate retries that should be billed; include a manual override and billing review step for edge cases.
